question: Will the Election Commission of India publish Andhra Pradesh's final SIR electoral roll on October 29 or 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: SIR final-roll publication dates in the 2026 round. Most states (Punjab and Telangana Oct 12, Karnataka and Delhi Oct 19) published on their last scheduled date. AP is an outlier with at least three extensions (Oct 9 -> Oct 16 -> Oct 30, plus an earlier original date), and the Oct 16 extension was announced only about 1-2 days ahead, so a late re-extension is a real risk. Factors favoring publication: hearings were 99.96% complete by early October; the SC (Oct 9) said SIR cannot delay local body polls, which reduces the incentive to keep extending; ECI is starting a new SSR cycle in 17 states/UTs (draft roll Nov 12). Repeated slippage and the Form-6 backlog keep a meaningful chance of a fourth extension. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.dossier:
- Deccan Chronicle (Oct 15, 2026): ECI under secretary Sandeep Kumar's communique to the AP CEO extends final SIR roll publication from Oct 16 to Oct 30 and the claims/objections disposal deadline from Oct 10 to Oct 22. No reason stated.
- AP extension history: an earlier original date (background says Sep 22), then Oct 9 -> Oct 16 (ECI full-bench decision Sep 30, ETV Bharat) -> Oct 30 (announced Oct 14-15, i.e. 1-2 days before the Oct 16 date). Meghalaya was also extended, to Oct 26.
- Reason given for the Oct 16 extension (Deccan Chronicle / web search summary): pending hearings on no-mapping and logical-discrepancy cases, plus pending Form 6/7/8 applications. Andhra Jyothy (Oct 2026): the Oct 30 extension is to clear claims and objections received up to Sep 10 and applications through Oct 12; CEO Vivek Yadav told DEOs to finish by Oct 22.
- Deccan Chronicle (about early Oct 2026): hearings done for 44.27 of 44.28 lakh notices (99.96%); 1,665 pending, 1,554 of them in Tirupati.
- Deccan Chronicle (about late Sep/early Oct 2026): registration of 1.76 lakh new voters (Form-6) pending.
- Other 2026 SIR states published final rolls on their scheduled dates: Punjab and Telangana Oct 12, Karnataka and Delhi Oct 19 (newsonair, web search results).
- Supreme Court (Oct 9, 2026, LiveLaw): SIR cannot delay AP local body polls; SIR rolls apply only if published before the election notification, otherwise old rolls apply.
- AP HC division bench (Oct 20, 2026, NIE): set aside a single-judge order; the State Election Commission can decide which rolls to use for local body polls.
- ECI (Oct 15-19, 2026): SSR announced for 17 states/UTs with qualifying date Jan 1, 2027 (draft Nov 12, final Jan 4, 2027); reports of internal disagreement among commissioners.
- Status quo: the schedule currently says publication on Oct 30.
- Base rate: in this 2026 SIR round, states whose schedule had been fixed mostly published on the last scheduled date. AP is the exception, with three or more slips. Each AP extension was announced shortly before the deadline.
- Resolves off: an official ECI/CEO AP notice of publication, or the 'SIR FinalRoll - 2026' download at voters.eci.gov.in for AP dated Oct 29-30 IST. Draft, supplementary or other roll releases do not count.
- Event window: Oct 29 00:00 IST -> Oct 30 23:59 IST per the criteria; as of Oct 20 the window has not opened yet (0% elapsed).
- Searched but not found: any news after Oct 15 about a further AP extension or about readiness for Oct 30; any prediction market on this question (none on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers).

calls.reasoning: Status quo: ECI's Oct 14 communique fixes AP SIR final publication for Oct 30, with claims and objections to be cleared by Oct 22. Base rate: once a final date is fixed, states in this round (Punjab, Telangana, Karnataka, Delhi) and earlier phases published on it. The remaining AP work is small (hearings 99.96% done by early Oct; the extension mostly covers Form 6/7/8 filed up to Oct 12), and the SC ruled the SIR cannot hold up local polls. Against that, AP has slipped 3-4 times, each time announced 1-2 days before the deadline, so the lack of news on Oct 20 is weak evidence; I put the chance of another slip at about 25-30%.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core facts: the Oct 30 date and Oct 22 disposal deadline from the Oct 14 communique, near-complete hearings, other states publishing on schedule, AP's repeated late extensions, no further extension reported, and no market. The disputes were minor. The extension count (3 vs 4 slips) could not be settled without web access and does not change the picture. Run 3's local body poll timing (poll Oct 28, count Oct 30) comes from one report I could not check; those polls use State Election Commission rolls, which that commission can choose, so I treat it as a weak risk either way. The main open question is a judgment: how much AP's slip history should discount the strong cross-state base rate. With the remaining workload small and the disposal deadline eight days before publication, I take about 71%. This is my own estimate from the evidence, not an average of the runs.
